name: A change the app and the server must make together

failureModes.prompt: Which side goes live first, the app or the server?
failureModes.why: the app reaches phones days after the server changes, so one of them is alone for a while

options.label: Together on the day
options.consequence: simpler to reason about, and impossible to guarantee

failureModes.provenBy: the previous app build exercised against the new server before the app is submitted

failureModes.prompt: Can we return everybody to the current experience without shipping a new release?
failureModes.why: an app release takes days to reach people, so a bad change without a switch stays live

options.label: A switch we control from the server
options.consequence: instant recovery, one more thing to maintain

options.label: Fix forward with a new release
options.consequence: less to build, days of exposure if it goes wrong

failureModes.recommended: A switch we control from the server
failureModes.provenBy: a recorded run turning the switch off and confirming the old experience returns without a release

failureModes.prompt: What happens to somebody who is halfway through the old journey when the new one goes live?
failureModes.why: a part-finished journey is the case nobody tests and everybody hits

options.label: Finish them on the old path
options.consequence: both paths run for a while, nobody is stranded

options.label: Move them to the new path
options.consequence: one path to maintain, some people lose their progress

failureModes.recommended: Finish them on the old path
failureModes.provenBy: a test that starts the old journey, switches the flag, and asserts the person can still finish

failureModes.prompt: Should results produced by the new version be kept apart from the current ones?
failureModes.why: mixing them makes it impossible to tell later which version produced what

options.label: Mark which version produced each record
options.consequence: a column now, clean comparison later

options.label: Store them together
options.consequence: simpler, and the two can never be separated again

failureModes.recommended: Mark which version produced each record
failureModes.provenBy: a query separating records by producing version after both have run

failureModes.prompt: Who should see the new experience before everybody does?
failureModes.why: the point of a staged switch is learning something before the whole audience arrives

options.label: A named internal group
options.consequence: safest, slowest to gather real signal

options.label: A small share of real users
options.consequence: real signal quickly, real people affected

failureModes.provenBy: a recorded check that a person outside the group receives the current experience

failureModes.prompt: What single number tells us the new version is better, not just different?
failureModes.why: without one agreed signal the switch stays on because nobody can argue it off

options.label: Judge it once it is live
options.consequence: no work now, and the argument never resolves

failureModes.provenBy: the measurement visible for both versions in the analytics tool before the switch is turned on
